# Guess Your Face — Full Documentation

> Real-time AI facial detection, 1:1 comparison, and face token analysis.
> Powered by Face++. Privacy-first, zero data retention.

## About Guess Your Face

Guess Your Face (GYF) is a modern web application built by REY-STTP that uses
the Face++ Cognitive Services API to analyze human faces in photographs. It
provides three real-time tools — Detect, Compare, and Analyze — wrapped in a
privacy-first architecture that processes every image in memory and never
writes user photos to disk, server, or database.

The product is the evolution (v2.0) of the original
[Facial-Expression-Detection-App](https://github.com/REY-STTP/Facial-Expression-Detection-App),
rewritten from scratch on Next.js 16 App Router with React 19 and TypeScript.

## Key features

### Detect (`/detect`)
- Multi-face detection in a single photo.
- 7 emotion spectra (Anger, Disgust, Fear, Happiness, Neutral, Sadness, Surprise)
  rendered as percentage-weighted animated bars.
- Comprehensive metrics: gender, age, smiling score, beauty score (male,
  female, average), 3D headpose (pitch, roll, yaw), and face quality score.
- Interactive bounding boxes drawn on the detected faces, indexed to result
  cards below.
- Auto-token handoff: detected face_tokens are saved to sessionStorage and
  clipboard so the user can instantly open the Analyze tool for deeper
  inspection without re-uploading.

### Compare (`/compare`)
- 1:1 face verification: upload two photos, decide whether they show the same
  person.
- Independent croppers for Photo 1 and Photo 2 with drag/pan/zoom.
- Confidence score visualization.
- Official Face++ false-positive thresholds (1e-3, 1e-4, 1e-5) shown as
  visual markers.
- Verdict: Same / Different based on the confidence vs threshold comparison.

### Analyze (`/analyze`)
- Deep attribute inspector for up to 5 face tokens in a single request.
- Modular attribute filters — pick exactly which dimensions to fetch:
  - Gender & Age
  - Emotion & Smiling
  - Face Quality & Beauty
  - Mouth Status: surgical mask, medical mask, mouth open, mouth occluded
  - Eye Status: open, closed, normal glasses, sunglasses, occlusion
- No re-upload required — paste face tokens from Detect results.

### Bilingual localization
- Full Indonesian (ID, default) and English (EN) support.
- Instant client-side language switch via React Context.
- Persistent preference stored in `localStorage` under key `gyf-locale`.
- Automatic browser-language detection on first visit.

### Built-in canvas cropper
- Interactive pan / drag / zoom before upload.
- Forces 1:1 aspect ratio to match Face++ face-detection best practices.
- Operates entirely client-side; the cropped blob is sent as multipart to
  the Next.js Route Handler.

## Tech stack

- Core framework: Next.js 16 (App Router) and React 19.
- Language: TypeScript 5.
- Styling: Tailwind CSS v4 with native CSS variables for theming.
- Typography: `@fontsource-variable/inter` (body), `@fontsource-variable/space-grotesk`
  (display), `@fontsource-variable/jetbrains-mono` (code/data).
- Icons: `@phosphor-icons/react`.
- Toasts: `sonner`.
- AI engine: Face++ Cognitive Services API (US region, v3).

## Architecture

```
[User selects photo]
  → [Interactive Canvas Cropper] (client-side)
  → [Next.js Client Tool component]
  → [POST multipart/form-data to /api/*]
  → [Next.js Route Handler: file validation + 2 MB cap]
  → [Inject FACEPP_API_KEY & FACEPP_API_SECRET server-side]
  → [HTTPS fetch to api-us.faceplusplus.com/facepp/v3/*]
  → [Friendly error mapping & sanitization]
  → [JSON result returned to client]
  → [Interactive FacePreview + EmotionBars + Metric cards]
  → [Optional: save face_token to sessionStorage/clipboard]
  → [Optional: open Analyze tool with tokens pre-filled]
```

The Face++ API key and secret are only ever read inside Route Handlers
(`app/api/*/route.ts`), never shipped to the client bundle.

## API routes

| Endpoint | Method | Body | Purpose |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `/api/detect` | POST | `multipart/form-data` (`file`) | Forward to Face++ `/detect`; return detected faces + attributes. |
| `/api/compare` | POST | `multipart/form-data` (`file1`, `file2`) | Forward to Face++ `/compare`; return confidence + thresholds. |
| `/api/analyze` | POST | `application/json` (`{ faceTokens, attributes }`) | Forward to Face++ `/face/analyze`; return deep attributes per token. |

All routes validate MIME type (`image/jpeg`, `image/png`), enforce the
2 MB Face++ limit, and translate Face++ error codes into localized Indonesian
or English messages via the `FRIENDLY_ERRORS` table in `lib/facepp.ts`.

## Privacy and security

1. **Zero Data Retention** — Uploaded images are processed directly in memory
   (Node `Buffer` / `FormData` stream) and forwarded to the Face++ API.
   They are never written to local disk, server filesystem, or any database.
2. **Protected credentials** — `FACEPP_API_KEY` and `FACEPP_API_SECRET` are
   exclusively read in server-side Route Handlers and never appear in the
   client bundle.
3. **Strict file validation** — MIME type check (`image/jpeg`, `image/png`)
   and a hard 2 MB size cap before forwarding to Face++.
4. **No analytics on user photos** — Guess Your Face does not run any
   analytics on uploaded images. The only telemetry is standard Vercel
   request metrics.

## How it works

1. **Upload & crop** — User drops or selects a photo. An interactive canvas
   cropper lets them frame the face in 1:1 with drag/pan/zoom.
2. **Client validation** — Before submitting, the browser checks the file
   type and size locally to give instant feedback.
3. **Server relay** — The client POSTs the file to a Next.js Route Handler
   (`/api/detect`, `/api/compare`, or `/api/analyze`).
4. **API credential injection** — Inside the Route Handler, the server
   reads `FACEPP_API_KEY` and `FACEPP_API_SECRET` from environment variables
   and appends them as multipart fields.
5. **Forward to Face++** — The Route Handler streams the request to
   `https://api-us.faceplusplus.com/facepp/v3/{endpoint}`.
6. **Sanitize & respond** — Errors are mapped to friendly messages via
   `lib/facepp.ts`. Successful JSON is returned to the client.
7. **Render** — The client component renders the response: bounding boxes
   on faces, percentage bars for emotions, metric cards for attributes,
   etc.
